Psychology from scratch

What psychology studies, its history, branches and methods.

Lesson 3. Basic and applied branches

1 · Lesson

Psychology is a very broad field, and it is usually organised in two large groups. The basic branches seek to understand how the mind works in general: perception, attention, memory, learning, language, thinking, emotion, motivation, development, personality, social psychology and biological foundations.

The applied branches use that knowledge to solve concrete problems: clinical and health psychology (assessing and treating psychological problems), educational psychology (learning and school), work and organisational psychology, legal and forensic psychology, social and community psychology, sport psychology, environmental, consumer, technology and human factors psychology, among others.

The two feed each other. Basic research on memory explains why spaced study works better; applied research checks whether that holds in a real classroom. And questions that arise in practice (why does this treatment work for some people and not others?) go back to the lab.

2 · Example

Human factors psychology studied why pilots confused similar-looking levers in the cockpit. The solution came from basic research on perception and attention: give each control a different shape to the touch. Today that principle is found in the design of cars, operating theatres and apps.

3 · Activity

Look at your day yesterday and note three situations in which an applied branch of psychology played a part (the design of a sign, an advert, a class, a medical appointment…). Which basic branch would be behind each one?
